description: Nucleus-level total RNA UMI count, calculated as the sum of gene-expression counts for the nucleus. Low values indicate limited RNA capture or library complexity, while unusually high values can be associated with multiplets. There is no universal recommended range; thresholds should be chosen from the per-GEM-well distribution and expected tissue complexity.

Nucleus-level base-10 logarithm of nCount_RNA, used to display RNA depth across its wide dynamic range. It has the same biological interpretation as nCount_RNA and is not an independent measurement; any QC guidance or threshold should normally be defined on the original nCount_RNA scale.

Nucleus-level percentage of RNA UMIs assigned to features whose names begin with MT-. Lower values are generally preferred because high values can reflect damaged nuclei or cytoplasmic contamination, although mitochondrial biology and nuclear preparations are tissue dependent. A 5% upper limit is used in a common PBMC example, but no universal cutoff exists and substantially different limits may be appropriate for other tissues.

Nucleus-level number of gene-expression features with at least one observed UMI. Low values indicate limited detected transcript diversity, while unusually high values can be associated with multiplets. Illustrative PBMC workflows retain approximately 200-2,500 detected genes, but nuclei, tissues, chemistries, and sequencing depths differ enough that per-GEM-well distributions should determine the useful range.

Nucleus-level RNA complexity measure calculated as log10(nFeature_RNA) divided by log10(nCount_RNA). Higher values generally indicate more detected features relative to RNA depth, but the measure becomes unstable for very low-count nuclei. No broadly established cutoff exists; compare its lower tail within GEM wells and interpret it jointly with nCount_RNA and nFeature_RNA.

Nucleus-level ATAC transcription start-site enrichment calculated by BPCells from fragment coverage around annotated transcription start sites. Higher values indicate a stronger open-chromatin signal relative to background. Values above 2 are commonly used as an illustrative minimum in single-cell ATAC workflows, with values above 3-4 often preferred, but the appropriate threshold depends on the implementation, reference annotation, tissue, and experiment.

Nucleus-level ratio of mononucleosomal to subnucleosomal ATAC fragments calculated from fragment lengths by BPCells. Lower values generally indicate a larger nucleosome-free contribution. Published single-cell ATAC examples have used upper limits ranging from approximately 4 to 10; the appropriate cutoff should be chosen from the experiment-specific distribution and fragment-length profile.

Nucleus-level Vireo posterior probability for the best singlet donor assignment. Values range from 0 to 1 and values closer to 1 indicate more confident singlet assignment. No universal probability cutoff is recommended; inspect posterior separation within the multiplexed experiment and use the inferred assignment class together with the probability.

Nucleus-level Vireo posterior probability for the most likely doublet assignment. Values range from 0 to 1 and values closer to 1 indicate stronger support for a donor doublet. No universal cutoff is recommended; interpret this probability relative to the singlet posterior and Vireo assignment for the same multiplexed experiment.

Nucleus-level Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted AMULET P value derived from the number of genomic loci covered by more than two fragments after high-overlap-site removal. Smaller values indicate stronger evidence of an ATAC multiplet; q-values below 0.05 are a conventional significance threshold, although a more stringent value may be appropriate when false-positive multiplet calls are costly.

Nucleus-level number of Cell Ranger ATAC fragments assigned to transcription start-site regions divided by the total number of ATAC fragments. Higher values generally indicate stronger regulatory signal around promoters. There is no broadly transferable per-nucleus cutoff because the value depends on the reference annotation and tissue; compare its lower tail across GEM wells and against Cell Ranger targeting diagnostics.

Nucleus-level number of Cell Ranger ATAC fragments overlapping called peak regions divided by the total number of ATAC fragments. Higher values indicate a larger fraction of fragments in accessible chromatin. Fractions below approximately 0.15-0.20 are often treated as low quality in illustrative single-cell ATAC workflows, but peak calling, tissue, and sequencing depth affect the suitable threshold.

display_name: Peak-region cut sites per ATAC fragment
description: Nucleus-level number of Cell Ranger ATAC cut sites in peak regions divided by the total number of ATAC fragments. The ratio can approach 2 because a fragment has two cut sites, so it is not a conventional bounded fraction. Higher values generally indicate stronger peak targeting, but no universal cutoff exists; compare the lower tail across GEM wells processed with the same definitions.

Nucleus-level number of Cell Ranger exonic RNA UMIs divided by the number of intronic RNA UMIs. This is a non-negative ratio rather than a bounded fraction; nuclear RNA commonly contains a larger intronic contribution than whole-cell RNA. No universal recommended range exists, so compare GEM wells prepared with the same protocol and investigate strong outliers in either direction.

Nucleus-level scDblFinder doublet score calculated separately within each GEM well from the GEX count matrix and GEX clusters. Higher scores indicate more doublet-like expression profiles, but the score is not a calibrated probability. scDblFinder estimates sample-specific decision thresholds, so use its doublet class rather than a universal numeric score cutoff and review unusually high-scoring clusters.

Nucleus-level sum of counts in the aggregation consensus-peak matrix. Low values indicate limited accessible-chromatin depth, while unusually high values can indicate multiplets. There is no universal recommended range because counts depend on peak definitions and the configured insertion or fragment-overlap counting mode; choose thresholds from the aggregation distribution.

Nucleus-level base-10 logarithm of nCount_ATAC, used to display consensus-peak accessibility depth across its wide dynamic range. It has the same interpretation and counting-mode dependence as nCount_ATAC; any QC guidance or threshold should normally be defined on the original nCount_ATAC scale.

Nucleus-level number of ATAC counts falling in genome blacklist regions, calculated with the configured peak-matrix counting mode. Lower values are generally preferred, but the absolute count scales with total ATAC depth. No universal absolute cutoff exists; interpret it jointly with nCount_ATAC and the blacklist fraction.

Nucleus-level ATAC blacklist count divided by nCount_ATAC. Lower values are generally preferred because high fractions indicate signal from regions prone to artefactual mapping. An upper limit near 0.05 is used in a common single-cell ATAC workflow, while stricter limits can be appropriate; confirm the denominator and blacklist definitions before transferring a threshold.

Nucleus-level nCount_ATAC divided by the Cell Ranger total ATAC fragment count. Higher values generally indicate stronger consensus-peak targeting, but the ratio can depend on whether peak counts represent insertions or fragment overlaps and therefore need not be bounded by 1. When it is comparable to fraction of fragments in peaks, values below approximately 0.15-0.20 can indicate low quality; otherwise select a distribution-based threshold within the configured counting mode.

Nucleus-level atac_peak_counts_frac divided by the fraction of the effective genome covered by the aggregation consensus peaks. Values above 1 indicate more peak-associated signal than expected from genomic coverage, and higher values generally indicate stronger enrichment. No universal QC cutoff exists because the value depends on peak coverage and counting mode; compare nuclei within the same aggregation.

Nucleus-level scDblFinder doublet score calculated separately within each GEM well from the ATAC consensus-peak count matrix and ATAC clusters. Higher scores indicate more doublet-like accessibility profiles, but the score is not a calibrated probability. scDblFinder estimates sample-specific decision thresholds, so use its doublet class rather than a universal numeric score cutoff and review unusually high-scoring clusters.

Nucleus-level relative ATAC contribution learned during weighted-nearest-neighbour integration from the RNA and ATAC neighbourhood structures. Values lie between 0 and 1, with values near 0.5 indicating similar relative contributions and values toward either extreme indicating modality dominance. This is an integration diagnostic rather than a direct quality measure, so no pass-fail cutoff is recommended; compare distributions across cell types and technical batches.
